sections.heading: Contextual Intelligence
sections.md: For the board — In plain terms, context is the moat. The Concierge ships eight capabilities no competitor has: Proactive context — acts before you ask; Cross-device memory — one context across rooms; Intent inference — reads the situation, not just words; Ambient sensing — presence, light, sound, motion; Routine learning — adapts to the household rhythm; Multi-user model — knows who is who; Privacy on device — sensitive inference stays local; Graceful fallback — degrades safely when unsure. Latency stays under ten milliseconds end to end.

sections.heading: The Competitive Field
sections.md: For the board — In plain terms, the competitive field is reactive — seven rivals, all waiting for a command: Belltower (reactive voice); Google Home (reactive voice); HomeKit (device control); Halcyon (closest — luxury voice); Umbra (installer automation); Quartzline (installer automation); SmartThings (hub + rules). Only Halcyon comes close, and it is still reactive.

sections.heading: Economics and Compliance
sections.md: For the board — In plain terms, the Concierge runs at household economics: CHF 0.58 per household per month, all in. eight safeguards keep it DSG-compliant under Swiss house policy: On-device inference — no raw audio leaves the home; Consent ledger — auditable opt-ins; Data minimisation — keep only what is used; Right to erasure — one-tap delete; Purpose binding — no secondary use; Local encryption — at rest + in transit; Access logging — who saw what, when; Swiss residency — data stays in CH.
